subject: Anthropology
title: Commodification
description: A short lesson to help you apply Commodification.

hook.text: Water was once free. Now it's bottled and sold. When something enters the market, its meaning changes forever.

buildup.text: Commodification turns things, services, or relationships into commodities that can be bought and sold on a market.

discovery.text: Marx saw commodification as central to capitalism. Labor becomes a product. People become replaceable inputs.

twist.text: Not everything should be a commodity. Organ sales, child labor, and paid friendships all provoke moral resistance.

climax.text: Commodification reveals capitalism's reach. When everything has a price, the question becomes: what should be priceless?

punchline.text: When you price everything, nothing is sacred.

quiz.question: What is commodification?
options: Turning things into commodities that can be bought and sold

details.summary: Commodification is the process of turning things, services, or relationships that were not previously for sale into market commodities. Labor, land, care, culture, and even body parts can be commodified when market logic expands into domains previously governed by social or moral norms.
details.whyItMatters: Commodification reveals market expansion as a cultural process, not a natural inevitability. Understanding what a society refuses to commodify reveals its deepest moral commitments about what should remain outside market logic.
takeaways: Commodification turns non-market things into market commodities
It occurs when market logic expands into social or moral domains
What societies refuse to commodify reveals their moral commitments

faq.question: What is an example of contested commodification?
faq.answer: Organ sales are prohibited in most countries because commodifying body parts violates deeply held moral beliefs. Surrogacy, blood donation, higher education, and clean water are all examples where societies debate whether market pricing is appropriate or morally corrosive.

faq.question: Can commodification be reversed?
faq.answer: Yes, through decommodification. Universal healthcare removes health from market logic. Public education decommodifies learning. Water re-municipalization takes drinking water out of private markets. Social movements often push to decommodify essentials that markets price out of reach.
